_comment: RMP-14/RMP-15. Rows taken from docs/plugin-v2/00-voice.md, 'Words to avoid -> say instead'. Read by hooks/voice_check.py. Two rows from that table are handled OUTSIDE this file, on purpose -- see prompts/COMMS.md: (1) 'hook' appears in the table twice (a marketing meaning and a technical one); only the marketing meaning can ever reach a customer, so the technical spelling is folded into the MCP/API/OAuth/token row instead of duplicated here. (2) 'workspace' is listed in 'allow', not 'avoid' -- the table asks for a one-time explanation, which a stateless per-message checker cannot enforce without re-flagging the word on every later, already-explained use (including the fixed trigger phrase 'switch workspace' the customer must be able to repeat). Flagging it always would break real, working customer lines for a rule this checker cannot express safely. RMP-159 part 2: 'the user', 'the checklist', 'now checking', 'now running', 'so I need to ask', 'no suggestion', 'recording the session' and 'probes' were added as narration markers -- internal narration a customer must never see. 'let me' from the same ticket's example list was deliberately left OUT: it collides with 'No, let me fix it', a real, already-tested customer-facing button label in own-instagram-account/SKILL.md (test_voice_rules_in_skills.py), so a blanket ban would flag good text. See prompts/COMMS.md for the full note. RMP-159 part 3: 'isn't set yet', 'is set yet' and 'neither is set' were added -- live dev examples narrated an internal field's state ('account_owner_type isn't set yet', 'Neither is set yet') even when the field name itself was hidden. A backtick-wrapped snake_case field name (e.g. `account_owner_type`) needed NO new row here -- hooks/voice_check_internal.py's existing generic snake_case rule (P1722) already catches it raw, backticks included; see test_voice_check_narration_part3.py for the falsifiable proof. RMP-159 part 4: live dev still leaked 'Closing the browser and logging the session now' ('logging' is a different verb from part 2's 'recording the session' row, which does not match it) and 'No revenue info saved yet, so both questions need asking' (part 2's 'so I need to ask' row is one fixed phrasing; 'saved yet, so' catches the shape regardless of what follows). A third leak, a website-reader sub-agent announcing "I'll wait for the website read to complete...", is fixed at the source in agents/website-reader.md instead -- a Stop-hook payload never sees a sub-agent's own sidechain transcript lines (voice_check_transcript.py's isSidechain filter), so the "i'll wait for" row here is defence-in-depth for the MAIN agent only. RMP-198: live dev (2026-09-26, wave 25, after RMP-107/RMP-159 part 6) still leaked 'All three connections passed. Closing the browser and recording the session start now.' (step 1, BEFORE record_session_start was even called) and 'Good, nothing missing. Ticking off the website step now.' (step 6, before record_checklist_step). 'recording the session' and 'closing the browser' already matched, so this is a live proof they were log-only, not a gap in the list -- the founder's own RMP-159 part 6 call ('fix at the source, keep the block off') stands: connection-check/SKILL.md and your-website/SKILL.md now tell the model explicitly to say nothing around these two calls. 'ticking off', 'step now' and 'session start' are added here as the missing safety-net rows for the exact new phrasing seen live -- the ticket's own wording was 'the step now', but the live line was 'Ticking off the WEBSITE step now' (the step's own name sits between 'the' and 'step'), so the row is the shorter 'step now' that still matches it and any other step name. RMP-200: live dev (2026-09-27, wave 27) leaked "This is the 4th retry, so I'll pass accept_partial:true now." while filling the website facts (your-website/SKILL.md section 7's retry loop) -- 'retry' and 'accept_partial' are the model's own internal instruction words for that loop, never customer wording, so both are new log-only rows here (the skill text itself was also strengthened at the exact call site, see SKILL.md). 'th retry' catches the 'Nth retry' shape ('4th retry', '5th retry', ...) that 'retry' alone would already flag anyway (defence in depth) -- ordinarily 'th' can never start a phrase match (it is always glued to a preceding digit, e.g. '4th', and the phrase matcher's left boundary refuses a preceding word character), so voice_check_internal.py's `_internal_phrase_pattern` special-cases this ONE term (same shape as its existing 'mcp' exception) to allow a digit right before 'th'. RMP-197 (step 8, founder comment 2026-09-27): the customer-facing ranked table's own header names columns "Niche" and "Easy to reach", so "Rank | Niche" and "Easy to reach" (both exact header phrases) are in 'allow' -- narrow, phrase-shaped exemptions, not a blanket allow for either bare word: 'niche'/'niches' and the metrics sense of 'reach' ("Your reach went up this week") both stay flagged everywhere else a reply might use them.

_internal_terms_comment: RMP-76 (founder: 'user should not know the backend on whats happening'). These are checked EVERYWHERE, including inside backticks -- the opposite of avoid_terms above -- so the model cannot dodge this rule by quoting a tool name as 'code'. Tool names are every mcp__plugin_rm-plugin-v2_reachmachine__* suffix the plugin's hooks can actually allow (from hooks/step_gate.py's _STEP_ALLOW and hooks/spend_gate.py's GATED_SUFFIXES), plus the two browser tools and the website-reader sub-agent name. The rest are system/architecture words. 'HTTP 4'/'HTTP 5' are deliberate PREFIXES so they catch any status code (see hooks/voice_check_internal.py). 'mcp' has one exception, also in that file: the literal '/mcp' the customer is told to type to sign in. P1722: hooks/voice_check_internal.py ALSO flags any lowercase_snake_case word on its own (no entry needed here for that shape) -- the rows below still list a few by name because a phrase like 'the plugin' or 'on my end' has no underscore for that generic rule to catch. RMP-159 part 5 (founder, 2026-09-26, 'Block and rewrite'): a row with no 'block' key, or 'block' missing/true, is a genuine internal name/field/tool -- hooks/voice_check.py now BLOCKS the reply and forces a same-turn rewrite when one of these leaks. A row with 'block': false is a narration-style marker (RMP-159 parts 2-4 below), never a real internal name -- those stay log-only exactly as before, per the founder's own scoping ('generic narration stays log-only'). 'pqr2' (RMP-1150's Positioning field, backend/app/mcp/creator_brief_reserved_keys_positioning.py) is a real reserved key with no underscore, so the generic snake_case rule cannot catch it -- named here instead.
